context: The lots array is the complete inventory; there are no other lots. All quantities are integer units; no rounding or conversion is applied. Eligible lots are those with expires_day >= ship_day, inclusive. Sort eligible lots by (expires_day, lot_id) ascending, comparing lot_id as a string. Allocate the requested quantity by taking as many units as possible from each lot in that order, moving to the next lot only after the current lot is exhausted or the requested quantity is filled. A lot from which zero units are taken is omitted from records. The records list only lots with positive allocations, in allocation order, each with the positive integer units taken. total is the unfilled remainder after all eligible lots are consumed: max(0, quantity - sum of units of all eligible lots). The destination must be a canonical relative .json path: no absolute path, no '.' or '..' segments, no backslashes, at most 200 characters, and every directory and the filename stem must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,31}; it must not contain or resolve through symlinks. Create the file at destination as UTF-8 JSON containing exactly {"records": [...], "total": ...} with object keys sorted, compact separators (no spaces), ASCII escapes, and one final newline; never overwrite an existing file. Return the same records and total along with the destination path.
